record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.original_question: If a real surface automorphism f has real entropy equal to the entropy of the complex map, must f be quasi-hyperbolic?

evidence.quote: Question 26. — If f is a real surface automorphism such that the entropy of fR is the same as the entropy of f, does it follow that f is quasi-hyperbolic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ be a polynomial automorphism (or more generally, a holomorphic automorphism of a real projective surface) defined over $\mathbb{R}$, so that $f$ preserves the real locus and restricts to a real-analytic diffeomorphism $f_{\mathbb{R}}$ of the real surface. Let $h(f)$ denote the topological entropy of $f$ acting on the complex points and let $h(f_{\mathbb{R}})$ denote the topological entropy of the restriction to the real points. Recall that $f$ is called quasi-hyperbolic on its set $J^*$ of saddle periodic points (the closure of saddle periodic points) if the tangent dynamics on $J^*$ admits no nonzero bounded orbits in the tangent bundle, equivalently, there is a dominated splitting with no neutral directions on $J^*$.

Question: Suppose $h(f_{\mathbb{R}}) = h(f)$. Must $f$ be quasi-hyperbolic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems on Hénon maps. Recent work (e.g., on real K3 automorphisms whose real entropy nearly matches the complex entropy) explores related phenomena but does not resolve the implication to quasi-hyperbolicity. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: A real K3 automorphism with most of its entropy in the real part
status_evidence.snippet: A real K3 surface can admit a real automorphism with topological entropy on complex points close to (but the question of equality and its consequences remains studied).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work investigates real surface automorphisms where real entropy equals/approaches the complex entropy, without resolving whether this forces quasi-hyperbolicity.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Plateaus of the Hénon Map (Arai)
status_evidence.snippet: Bedford–Smillie's notion of quasi-hyperbolicity for Hénon maps; related to maximal-entropy hyperbolic automorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-hyperbolicity is the standard property in question; its equivalence with the maximal-real-entropy condition is not established.
